source.title: Beyond Benign Overfitting in Nadaraya-Watson Interpolators
source.authors: Daniel Barzilai; Guy Kornowski; Ohad Shamir

record.file_problem: No apparent garbling or cutoff; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study proves and illustrates overfitting profiles for a Nadaraya-Watson interpolator as its distance exponent β varies. It does not test double descent over model size, epochs, sample size near an interpolation threshold, or effective complexity.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-error results while varying β, noise, and data settings, but β is a bandwidth-like exponent, not the size, training time, or sample-size axis in the claim. Those results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. The experiments that vary sample count do not explicitly state that more data raises test error near an interpolation threshold. Values visible only in the omitted plots are not inferred.
record.test_reason: The study analyses an interpolating Nadaraya-Watson estimator whose error is studied as its distance exponent β varies. Every β interpolates the training set, so β is a locality or bandwidth parameter, not a capacity axis crossing an interpolation threshold. No result tracks error over model size, epochs, or samples near an interpolation threshold, or against an effective-complexity measure. Belkin et al. 2019a appears only as background motivation in the introduction.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude the NW interpolator is tempered for β>d, benign at β=d, and can be catastrophic for β<d. They also conclude that overestimating intrinsic dimension is preferable to underestimating it; the dependence on intrinsic dimension for manifold data is stated as a conjecture.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and simulates a Nadaraya-Watson interpolator while varying its distance exponent β; it does not use the model-size, epoch, or sample-size sweeps of the double-descent claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported profile depends on β relative to dimension, label-noise level, data distribution, and—in the additional spherical experiment—input-noise variance.

fits_no_version.finding: Asymptotic clean error of the NW interpolator is tempered (Õ(p)) for β>d and benign at β=d. For β<d there is a constructed instance whose error is bounded below independently of p (Thms 4.1, 5.1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For a single interpolating estimator, varying a bandwidth-like exponent moves overfitting non-monotonically from catastrophic through benign to tempered.

fits_no_version.finding: On 1-D, spherical and MNIST 0/1 data, error is asymmetric in β: overly large β hurts less than overly small β. The best β tracks intrinsic dimension (β=2 on S², β≈8 on MNIST).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the NW interpolator, overestimating intrinsic dimension when setting β is less harmful than underestimating it.

record.problems: The experimental error curves are presented in figures; the text gives qualitative summaries rather than the full plotted values. The dimension-dependent conclusions for lower-dimensional manifolds are described as a conjecture rather than formalized.
record.rows_left_out: The paper also reports experiments varying sample count in Figures 3–5 and input-noise variance in Figure 6. The text does not state that increasing sample count raises test error near an interpolation threshold, and Figure 6 concerns input noise and the best β rather than a double-descent peak; these were not extracted as claim-bearing rows.

untested.parts: Test error versus deep-network size and a peak near the interpolation threshold; no networks are trained.
Test error over training epochs; the estimator has no training dynamics.

Whether more samples raise test error near an interpolation threshold. The m-sweeps in Figs 3–5 are of an always-interpolating estimator, and the text says only that the β-asymmetry grows more pronounced with m.
Risk improving again past the interpolation point as capacity grows. The β-sweep is not a capacity sweep across interpolation.
Label-noise-driven peak, multiple descents, or removal under optimal regularization. Label noise p is varied, but only along β, with no double-descent peak.
Recounting effective parameters to turn the second descent into a U-shaped curve.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation (cites_only) and tranche (T6) are confirmed. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The study belongs to the benign/tempered/catastrophic overfitting taxonomy literature (Mallinar et al.), not to double-descent tests. Because the estimator interpolates for every β and m, there is no interpolation threshold on any axis studied.

versions.untested_parts: Model-wise test-error curve over deep-network size and its peak near the size that just fits training data.
Whether increasing sample size near an interpolation threshold raises test error.
Risk as capacity grows past interpolation across model classes.
Whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across axes.
Whether a double-descent peak is driven by noise or variance, splits into multiple peaks, or disappears under optimally tuned regularization.
Whether effective parameter counting turns a second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: Nadaraya-Watson interpolator ĥβ
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical asymptotic clean classification error bound for β>d.
rows.value: C1(β/d)·p^c(β/d) ≤ L(ĥβ) ≤ C2(β/d)·log_{1−d/β}(1/p)·p; in particular, L(ĥβ)=Õ(p).
rows.note: This is an asymptotic bound for the exponent regime, not a curve over model capacity, training time, or sample size.

rows.subject: Nadaraya-Watson interpolator ĥβ
rows.operation_detail: Theoretical asymptotic lower bound for a constructed distribution and target function when β<d.

conditions.value: constructed density and target function satisfying Assumption 3.1

rows.value: L(ĥβ) ≥ C2·c(β,d), a positive constant independent of p.
rows.note: The result concerns sensitivity to β and a constructed setting; it is not a double-descent curve.

rows.subject: Nadaraya-Watson interpolator ĥβ
rows.operation_detail: Sweep β while varying label-flip probability on one-dimensional synthetic data.
rows.value: For β<1, error quickly reaches 0.1 in all tested noise cases; for β>1, deterioration is controlled by p.
rows.uncertainty: 50 runs; average error plotted with a 95% confidence interval.
rows.note: The prose reports the qualitative findings; exact curve values are not stated in the text.

rows.subject: Nadaraya-Watson interpolator ĥβ
rows.operation_detail: Sweep β while varying label-flip probability on spherical synthetic data.

conditions.value: uniformly sampled on S²⊂R³ with the spherical-cap labeling in Eq. (5)

rows.value: The text reports the same asymmetry: overly large β is more forgiving than overly small β, especially at low noise; the optimal benign exponent is β=2.
rows.uncertainty: 50 runs; average error plotted with a 95% confidence interval.
rows.note: The reported β=2 corresponds to the sphere's intrinsic dimension.

rows.subject: Nadaraya-Watson interpolator ĥβ
rows.operation_detail: Sweep β while varying label-flip probability on MNIST 0/1 data.
rows.value: The text reports the same asymmetric phenomenon; the optimal exponent is roughly β≈8.
rows.uncertainty: 50 runs; average error plotted with a 95% confidence interval.
rows.note: The text contrasts β≈8 with the 784-pixel extrinsic dimension.
